title: Hourly telemetry playlist and rollback gates — Oct 2025 notes
summary: Working draft: concise hourly telemetry watchlist, preflight and immediate rollback gates for the Oct 2025 feature push. Purpose: give on-call and release conductor a small, actionable signal set + clear decision gates for rolling forward vs rollback during first 24h.
preflight-checklist:
(T-48 to T-0)
- Verify canary config applied: 2% traffic lane mapped to canary model v3.1.
- Smoke tests green from staging (end-to-end prompts, embedding recall).
- Load simulation run for expected burst (peak QPS * 1.3) with 95th latency under target.
- Telemetry dashboards pinned & shared with release channel.
- Alert routing confirmed: SEV1 -> SRE, SEV2 -> Release conductor -> Product.
- Backup route: model variant v3.0 pinned for immediate fallback; traffic-shift runbook preloaded.
- Ops rota: named responders for 0–12h and 12–48h windows.
- Slack + PagerDuty escalation messages prepared and reviewed.
- Canary kill-switch and traffic ramp script tested in dry-run.
hourly-rollout-calendar-first-12h:
T+0 (00:00) — Launch canary at 2%
T+1 (01:00) — Verify 1st hour metrics: user-facing latency, tail P99, error rate, token drop rate.
T+2 (02:00) — Decision checkpoint: if all green, bump to 5%. If small regressions (<=20% relative increase) hold and observe another hour.
T+3 (03:00) — Ramp to 15% if signals stable for two consecutive checkpoints.
T+4 (04:00) — Ramp to 30% and run smoke synthetic queries for complex flows.
T+6 (06:00) — Full-metrics review (team sync): perf, cost estimate delta, caller timeouts.
T+8 (08:00) — Ramp to 60% if stable, else open incident and follow rollback matrix.
T+12 (12:00) — Decision: finish ramp to 100% or pause and keep a staged rollout for remainder of day.
Notes: calendar assumes 1-hour steady-state observation windows; emergency rollback may be triggered immediately if critical signals cross hard thresholds.
telemetry-playlist-and-thresholds:
Primary signals (must monitor every 5 minutes):
- 95th latency (service-side, excluding network): hard gate = > 1.8x baseline for 5m -> immediate rollback review; severe = > 2.5x -> rollback.
- 99th latency: soft gate = > 2.0x baseline (observe 2 intervals) -> hold ramp.
- Error rate (5xx from inference service): hard gate = > 0.5% absolute or 3x baseline relative increase -> immediate rollback.
- Token drop / OOM events: any occurrence -> immediate rollback and hotfix pipeline.
- Model quality regression (eval-set BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-sim): if drop > pre-agreed threshold (see CONFLUENCE-1234) -> halt and investigate.
- Upstream caller timeouts / client-side errors: if increased by >15% -> investigate routing/backpressure.
Secondary signals (15m cadence):
- Cost per token uplift > 20% -> product review, consider throttles/quantization change.
- Disk / GPU memory pressure > 75% -> preemptive scale-out or reduce batch size.
- Queue depth growth (sustained > 2x baseline) -> throttle / hold ramp.
Notes: telemetry panels should include short-run deltas (1h vs baseline) and rolling 5m windows for gate decisions.
rollback-gates-and-actions:
Hard rollback gates (trigger immediate rollback and SEV alert):
- P99 latency > 2.5x baseline sustained for 5 minutes.
- 5xx error spike (absolute > 0.5%) or repeated OOM in serving hosts.
- Model output quality severe regression for critical eval prompts.
Action steps after a hard gate fires:
1) Release conductor executes traffic-shift to pinned fallback (v3.0) via runbook script.
2) Notify SRE + Product + Customer Success in the release channel.
3) Create incident ticket and collect PID (trace ids, example requests).
4) Post-mortem checklist: collect core dumps, stack traces, profiling captures.
Soft rollback gates (pause/rate-hold and deeper triage):
- P99 latency 1.8–2.5x baseline or steady queue growth.
- Error rate 1.2–3x baseline but < hard threshold.
Action: hold further ramps, open triage (engineering, infra, product), run diagnostic synthetic queries, attempt conservative mitigations (reduce batch size, enable additional nodes), re-evaluate at next checkpoint.
communications-playbook:
Before launch: short note to #release-ops with launch time, owner, and kill-switch steps.
On checker failures: one-line update to channel with status (OK / HOLD / ROLLBACK), primary metric failing, action taken.
If rollback: use template: 'ROLLBACK: <release-tag> -> <fallback-tag>. Triggered by <metric> at <time>. Action: traffic-shift complete. Incident: <link>'.
Customer comms: Customer Success to prepare proactive note if rollback expected to affect SLAs (>30 minutes degradation).
Post-incident: 1-hour status digest then 24-hour follow-up with timeline; attach telemetry snapshots and initial hypothesis.
release-notes-draft-short:
Release v3.1 — Oct 2025 (draft)
Highlights:
- Model: upgraded generation model (v3.1) with improved long-context coherency — target tasks: multi-turn assistants, code synthesis.
- Observability: added per-route latency breakdowns and token accounting in console.
- Ops: new canary traffic-shift tooling and automated rollback script.
Bugfixes:
- Fix for rare KV-cache desync causing repeated token repeats on long contexts.
Known issues (investigating):
- A small subset of complex prompts may show increased P99 latency when using large-batch inference on older GPU types. Mitigation: fallback to smaller batches for those routes.
Notes: keep this header visible on release page; final copy to be sanitized for public release notes after post-launch review.
